This is the most scenic drive in South Dakota and almost no one talks about it 👇

Needles Highway is a 14 mile drive inside Custer State Park, South Dakota that winds through granite spires, one-lane rock tunnels, and hairpin turns.

It’s in the Black Hills between Custer and Mt Rushmore and it’s one of the best road trips in the USA if you love dramatic landscapes.

📍 SAVE THIS FOR YOUR BLACK HILLS TRIP:
Must stop along the drive:
Needles Eye Tunnel - one lane tunnel carved through granite
Cathedral Spires Overlook - best photo spot
Sylvan Lake for hiking & picnics
Hike if you have time:
Cathedral Spires Trail, 1.6 miles out & back to the base of granite walls
Sunday Gulch Trail, 3.9 mile loop from Sylvan Lake with ladders + scrambles
Little Devil’s Tower Trail, 3.8 miles with views of Black Elk Peak

Best time to go: Summer to early fall. Go early morning or late afternoon, less traffic, better light. Winter = road closures.

Pro tip: Drive slow, road is VERY narrow. Vehicles over 8ft wide / 12ft tall won’t fit through tunnels. Pair it with Wildlife Loop Road in Custer State Park.

LAKE LOUISE, ALBERTA, Complete 2025/2026 Guide:

PRO TIP: Do the 25km Big Loop - Agnes > Beehive > Six Glaciers > Louise in one day if you’re fit.

MUST DO (non-hike):
•  Canoe Lake Louise at 8am - turquoise is brightest, no wind, red canoe photo
•  Moraine Lake Rockpile - 0.8km for Valley of Ten Peaks
•  Bow Valley Parkway at dusk - grizzly + elk spotting

This lake is at 5,680ft and gets its color from glacial rock flour. No filter.

caption:
Steal my Mount Rainier itinerary 🏔️ I did the research so you don’t have to

Save this if Washington is on your 2026 bucket list. This park has it all wildflower meadows, glaciers, alpine lakes, and waterfalls that don’t even look real.

My perfect 1-2 day route 👇

PARADISE SIDE (Don’t skip this)
Skyline Trail - 5.5 miles - The BEST hike in the park. 360° views of Rainier, glaciers, marmots, and endless wildflowers in late July/Aug.

Nisqually Vista Trail - 1.2 miles - All the glacier views with almost no effort.

Myrtle Falls - 1 mile - The iconic postcard view of Rainier + waterfall. Go before 9am.

SUNRISE SIDE (Best for fewer crowds)
Fremont Lookout - 5.6 miles - Fire lookout with insane ridge views. Feels like you’re on top of the PNW.

Sunrise Nature Trail - 1.5 miles - Easy meadow loop if you’re short on time.

MY FAVORITE LOOP NEAR THE PARK:
Naches Peak Loop - 3.5 miles at Tipsoo Lake - Wildflowers + perfect lake reflection of Rainier. This is THE photo spot.

Add these if you have time: Christine Falls, Narada Falls, Reflection Lakes, Bench & Snow Lakes, Silver Falls

PRO TIPS to save you time:
1.  Paradise entrance gets full by 9:30am in summer - enter early
2.  Late July to mid-Aug is peak wildflower season
3.  No timed entry needed for 2026, but parking is brutal

caption:
What is that one place you dream about?
Me: Hallstatt 

🏔️ Hallstatt, Austria, the real-life village people swear inspired Frozen ✨
Tucked between the Austrian Alps and a glassy lake, Hallstatt looks unreal in person. Pastel houses stacked up the hillside, snow-capped peaks behind them, and one of the prettiest lakeside views in all of Europe.
If you’re planning where to go, here’s the practical version 👇

🚂 How to get to Hallstatt from Salzburg: easiest as a day trip train + ferry gets you there in about 2.5 hours, and the boat arrival is the view everyone photographs. 

🏔️ Best things to do in Hallstatt: the Skywalk viewpoint, the Salt Mine (oldest in the world), and just getting lost on the lakeside streets early before the crowds. 

🛏️ Where to stay in Hallstatt: book directly in the village if you want it empty at sunrise day trippers clear out by evening and it’s a completely different place.

Fun fact: there’s a full scale Hallstatt replica in China because the real one is that photogenic 🇦🇹

caption:
Fall in Zion National Park feels like stepping into a golden fairytale 🍂✨

Towering red cliffs, cottonwood trees turned gold, and that crisp canyon air in October if fall in Utah is not on your bucket list, it should be.

I made this fall Zion guide so you don’t miss peak colors 👇

WHEN TO GO FOR FALL COLORS:
Peak fall foliage in Zion is mid-October to early November. Best color is along the Virgin River, Pa’rus Trail, and Zion Canyon Scenic Drive.

MUST-DO FALL HIKES:
Angels Landing (permit required), The Narrows bottom-up, Emerald Pools, The Watchman Trail, and Pa’rus Trail for easy fall colors.

WHERE TO STAY & LOGISTICS:
Stay in Springdale for walking distance to the park. Book 6-9 months ahead for October. Fall shuttle runs 8am-6pm, parking fills by 9am, arrive early. Pack layers: 70°F days, 40°F mornings.

BEST PHOTO SPOTS FOR GOLDEN HOUR:
Canyon Junction Bridge, Court of the Patriarchs viewpoint, Pa’rus Trail at sunset, and Virgin River reflections.

caption:
POV: you found one of the wildest beaches in the Pacific Northwest 🌊🪵

Rialto Beach in Olympic National Park feels like stepping into a moody coastal movie, towering sea stacks, massive driftwood, crashing Pacific waves and rugged Washington coastline in every direction.

Located near La Push on the Olympic Peninsula, Rialto Beach is one of the best beaches to visit in Washington State and a must-stop on any Olympic National Park road trip.

Walk along the shoreline toward Hole in the Wall, explore tide pools during low tide, photograph the dramatic sea stacks and stay for one of the most unforgettable sunsets on the Washington coast.

A few Rialto Beach tips:
🌊 Check the tide schedule before hiking
🥾 Wear waterproof shoes with good grip
📸 Visit early morning or around sunset for dreamy light
🌧️ Bring a rain jacket, the weather changes quickly
🪵 Never turn your back on the ocean or climb unstable driftwood

caption:

Olympic National Park is one of the most diverse national parks in the USA, where you can hike through an ancient temperate rainforest, explore dramatic Pacific Northwest beaches, chase waterfalls, and stand among mountain peaks, all in one trip.

🥾 Best hikes and places to visit in Olympic National Park:

🌿 Hoh Rain Forest
• Hall of Mosses Trail :0.8-mile loop
• Spruce Nature Trail : 1.2-mile loop
Walk beneath moss covered trees in one of the most magical rainforests in Washington State.

🏔️ Hurricane Ridge
• Hurricane Hill Trail : 3.4 miles round trip
One of the best Olympic National Park hikes for panoramic mountain views, wildflowers, and possible wildlife sightings.

🌊 Rialto Beach
• Hole in the Wall Trail : around 3.3 miles round trip
Explore sea stacks, driftwood-covered shores, tide pools, and one of the most beautiful beaches on the Olympic Peninsula. Check the tide chart before hiking!

💧 Sol Duc Valley
• Sol Duc Falls Trail : 1.6 miles round trip
A short forest hike leading to one of the most iconic waterfalls in Olympic National Park.

💙 Lake Crescent
• Marymere Falls Trail : 1.8 miles round trip
• Mount Storm King : around 4 miles round trip, steep and challenging
Stop for the crystal clear lake views, then choose between a peaceful waterfall hike or an adventurous climb.

🌅 More places to add to your Olympic Peninsula itinerary:
Ruby Beach, Second Beach, Kalaloch Beach, Tree of Life, Madison Falls, Lake Quinault Rainforest and Cape Flattery.

caption:
🏔️ Hallstatt, Austria the fairytale village that looks straight out of Disney’s Frozen ✨🇦🇹

Nestled between the Austrian Alps and the crystal clear Hallstätter See, Hallstatt is one of the most beautiful places in Austria and easily one of the most scenic villages in Europe. From colorful lakeside houses and mountain views to centuries of history, this UNESCO World Heritage village feels almost too perfect to be real.

Planning a trip to Hallstatt? Save these tips 👇

🚂 How to get to Hallstatt:
The easiest day trip from Salzburg is by train + ferry. The ferry arrival gives you the iconic postcard view that made Hallstatt famous worldwide.

🌅 Best time to visit Hallstatt:
Arrive before 8 AM or stay overnight. Most tour buses arrive later in the morning, and sunrise is when Hallstatt feels truly magical.

🏔️ Best things to do in Hallstatt:
• Hallstatt Skywalk for panoramic alpine views
• Visit the world’s oldest Salt Mine
• Wander the charming old town streets
• Take a lakeside walk along Hallstätter See
• Rent a boat for stunning lake views
• Explore nearby viewpoints and hidden photo spots

🛏️ Where to stay:
Book a hotel directly in Hallstatt if your budget allows. Once the day trippers leave, the village becomes peaceful, quiet, and even more beautiful.

✨ Fun fact: Hallstatt became so famous that an entire replica village was built in China.
